speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance. To help me determine the cause, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or came on gradually, and are you currently lying down or moving when they occur?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

Thank you for the details; the fact that your dizziness is a constant, low-grade spinning sensation rather than strictly position-triggered makes me reconsider the classic BPPV diagnosis. Given your age and the recent cold, could you clarify if you have noticed any hearing loss, tinnitus, or ear fullness alongside these symptoms? Also, did you experience a recent head injury or fever?
